newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germans unveil memorial to Nazi euthanasia victims.
newsitem.headline: Germans unveil memorial to Nazi euthanasia victims.

text.p: The German town of Brandenburg unveiled a memorial to the victims of Hitler's euthanasia policy on Sunday at the site where the Nazis built their first permanent gas chamber to eradicate the sick and the handicapped.

Information plaques and stones marking the outline of the buildings will tell visitors of the fate of 9,000 men, women and children gassed to death because their incurable conditions meant they did not fit into the Nazi concept of a master race.
"Brandenburg saw the start of the attempt to eliminate whole groups of people whose lives were inhumanly labelled 'unworthy to be lived'," state science minister Steffen Reiche said.
Historians estimate that at least 100,000 people were killed between 1940 and 1945 in an operation initiated by Hitler himself, in six institutions disguised as nursing homes.
As the first of these, Brandenburg provided the experience which allowed the others to be set up.

Hitler prepared the ground for his campaign, called Operation T4, with propaganda films which portrayed the mentally handicapped and the incurably ill as "useless mouths to feed" who could be relieved of their suffering by a "sensible doctor".

The campaign was nominally ended in 1941 after churches in particular found out about it and protested. But in practice the patients continued to be killed, by starvation, lethal injections or tablets, instead of being gassed.
